summary:
Świętokrzyskie was the fifth of the voivodeships adopting a regional "anti-LGBT ideology" resolution by June 2020, completing the configuration that at peak covered about a third of national territory across roughly 100 municipalities and five regions. Located in the same eastern conservative bloc as Łódzkie and Lubelskie, its resolution was annulled or repealed in the 2020–2021 court-and-EU-pressure wave.

No march ban, violence episode, or holdout municipality comparable to the Subcarpathian or Podlaskie findings is documented at the voivodeship scale. The visitor-facing signal is the regional declaration's intent to exclude LGBTQ public presence and the social climate of the PiS heartland belt; the formal legal document is now absent.

Score of 0.48 sits 0.04 below the national 0.52, identical to Łódzkie (0.48) on shared evidence: both are resolution-carrying voivodeships in the eastern bloc without unit-specific enforcement or violence findings beyond the declaration itself. Above Lublin (0.45), which additionally contains Świdnik, Poland's first-ever anti-LGBT municipal resolution.

sources.summary: Encyclopedia overview of Poland's 'LGBT-free zones': by June 2020 about 100 municipalities and five voivodeships - Swietokrzyskie the last adopter completing the five - had passed resolutions covering a third of Poland; symbolic and unenforceable but stigmatising, Ordo Iuris-lobbied; every such resolution had been repealed or court-invalidated by spring 2025.

Legal-overview article on the rise and fall of Poland's LGBT-free zones: between 2019 and 2025 more than 100 local governments adopted 'LGBT ideology'-free resolutions or Ordo Iuris-drafted family-rights charters covering roughly a third of the country at peak; the documents created no criminal penalties but symbolically sidelined LGBT residents from civic life; the national human-rights commissioner's litigation led courts to strike them down as unconstitutional, the EU threatened to freeze billions in regional funds, and the last remaining zone was abolished in spring 2025.

tangentialFactors: The regional resolution targeted 'LGBT ideology' broadly rather than trans people as such; with the document gone, what remains visitor-facing is the declaration-era civic climate of the ruling party's heartland belt, not any unit-specific instrument.
